events.what: Aires and Kahn prove asymptotic lower bounds on the balance constant delta(P) for posets of large width (delta(P) -> 1/2 under width/minimal-element conditions; delta(P) >= 1/e - o(1) under weaker width conditions)
Aires and Kahn study variance vs. range for linear extensions and balancing extensions in posets of bounded width
Gupta's exhaustive census verifies the Gold Partition Conjecture (hence 1/3-2/3) for all posets on at most 14 elements
events.ai_basis: Claude Code and Codex 'were used extensively for software development and optimization, computational experiment design, literature discovery, and drafting and editing the manuscript.'

judgement.doubts: The Aires-Kahn delta >= 1/e - o(1) result could arguably be read as settling a case (large posets meeting a width condition); coded bound since it moves the constant on restricted classes rather than settling a clean restriction of the bullet. Either way the tier is below 'claimed' and the AI role is none. The Gupta census is finitely many instances (F4), and its AI disclosure describes coding, experiment design and drafting, not mathematics in the result (F9), so it would be 'none' even if it counted. Aires-Kahn acknowledgements were not read in full by the researcher.

outcome_prefix: In two 2025 preprints, Aires and Kahn prove new asymptotic lower bounds on the balance constant delta(P) for posets of large or bounded width; the general conjecture stays open.
